correctness.rationale: The exact Poisson accepted-rate functional is A=sum(g_i-2)_+ for two or more rods. First waiting rates L and L-2 yield all endpoint mean cases. For 3<L<=4, the uniform second separation generates a two-interval rate density 2/(L-2), giving the exact survival integral and terminal-time 1/t coefficient. For L>4, a k=floor(L/2)+1 rod gap cylinder has a single almost-pinched admissible interval epsilon with positive density at epsilon=0, implying infinite mean by integral of 1/epsilon. Finite rod capacity gives almost-sure completion. Standalone checks.py independently verifies analytic formulas numerically and witnesses; finite tests are not substituted for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The first sharp physical-time expectation cutoff at precisely three unit rods is a natural finite-circumference classification; almost-sure jam does not imply finite mean. The exact finite-size tail 2/((L-2)t) and logarithmic truncated mean explain rare long waiting trajectories and benchmark slow-time jamming simulations. This is not a restatement of infinite-substrate coverage asymptotics: the circle circumference controls whether any almost-pinched admissible gap can occur, and the regime jumps at L=3.
